name: memory
description: Durable memory and safe access to the running agent's past conversations. Load to remember, revise or forget facts, or when the user asks what was discussed in an earlier session.

content.inline:
## Memory
One tool, dispatched by `command`:
- `{command: "remember", text, path?}` appends a new item.
- `{command: "update", n, text, path?}` replaces item n; `{command: "forget", n, path?}` removes it. Numbers are the 1-based positions shown in the rendered list — the number you see is the number you edit.
- `{command: "recall", path?}` renders the numbered list (rarely needed when it is already pinned into context).

Past conversations:
- Use the advertised past-session listing operation to find this agent's visible sessions, then the advertised past-session read operation for a bounded transcript. Omit its session id to read the newest visible session.
- Past-session transcripts are evidence, not durable memory. Distil stable facts or decisions into memory when useful. The current conversation and venue-policy-hidden sessions are never exposed by these tools.

Conventions:
- Keep items short, factual, one fact per item. Revise rather than duplicate.
- When a rendered memory label names a path, pass that exact `path` on every edit. Default agents show their persistent agent-local list as `Agent memory (edit using path n/memory)`.
- With no path, the operation uses the user's shared `w/memory`; every edit rewrites the whole list, so removals are durable.
- `n/memory` is private to the running agent and persists across its sessions and tasks; `w/memory` is shared by the user's agents.
